body:
FULL RED-TEAM VERDICT

Bottom line: do not make “live public fact-checking on a PWA evidence screen” the MVP center. The dependable and valuable core is a presenter copilot: rehearsed deck intelligence, private live cues, pre-approved evidence, and post-session audit. Public live web cards should remain an experiment until they beat a static baseline on comprehension without increasing distraction or error.

A. PWA/multi-display premise
- PWA installation is packaging, not capability. It grants no extra screen placement, fullscreen, popup, microphone, or connectivity privilege.
- The actual dependable baseline is ordinary browser windows: user opens one stage, drags it, clicks fullscreen. Window Management is a Chromium-desktop enhancement; getScreenDetails can be denied; window.open can return null, positions are clamped, each new window needs a gesture; cross-origin stage needs its own fullscreen gesture.
- Mirror detection is particularly treacherous: mirrored output is not a distinct screen to the API, and the app cannot prove OBS/screen sharing/HDMI topology. Calling privacy “guaranteed” is false.
- Therefore copy must be: “guided dual-display setup; automatic placement on supported Chromium desktops.” If “automatic on all Windows presentation machines” is required, PWA-alone fails; use an Electron/native launcher only for deployment-controlled venues, or accept guided manual setup.

B. Five-second live-web premise
- Five seconds can buy plausible retrieval, not trustworthy verification. Real-world claim checking is multi-stage: claim decomposition, raw retrieval, fine evidence retrieval, summarization, judgment. NAACL 2024 explicitly describes a five-component realistic pipeline and says even reliable summaries may not be complete evidence sets: https://aclanthology.org/2024.naacl-long.196/
- Search can actively worsen judgment. Nature reported that searching to evaluate misinformation can land users in “data voids” containing corroboration from low-quality sources: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06883-y
- Google Fact Check API only searches previously published ClaimReview material; it cannot verify a novel utterance, and Google does not create/endorse those checks: https://developers.google.com/fact-check/tools/api/reference/rest/
- Snippets, generated URLs, or a semantic-match score must never become “SUPPORTED.” The bottleneck is source/claim fit, temporal validity, units/entities, source authority, rights/privacy/ACL—not model inference time.
- Correct SLA: p95 final-utterance -> PRIVATE eligible candidate <=5s, with timeout -> no card. Measure STT endpointing separately. Public approval/render is a separate SLO. Hard or novel claims should often yield zero results; abstention is success.
- Useful alternative: upload-time evidence compilation plus live retrieval only from the frozen approved bundle. External web search runs asynchronously into presenter-only “needs review,” or during Q&A when a deliberate pause exists.

C. Audience evidence-screen premise
- There is no established benefit merely from adding another public screen. Split-attention theory warns against requiring people to integrate spatially separated sources; a meta-analysis and handbook literature support integrating rather than separating related representations: https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/cambridge-handbook-of-multimedia-learning/splitattention-principle-in-multimedia-learning/194CBCD1A3C911116CCB5F403AC7E415
- Evidence cards arrive after the sentence, pull gaze away from the speaker/current slide, may expire before reading, and can publicly amplify a false or contentious claim. Three cards every five seconds is a notification machine, not a presentation aid.
- Contrary nuance: extra visual layers can help accessibility when complementary and synchronized. A 2025 PLOS experiment found no significant comprehension difference between subtitles, interpreting, and both, though combined mode reduced measured effort/stress in that narrow multilingual setup: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0330692 . This does NOT generalize to unrelated evidence cards; it argues for captions/number-name reinforcement before an auxiliary fact stream.
- Safer public design: one integrated, presenter-invoked “evidence moment,” replacing or occupying a reserved region of the current slide—not a continuously mutating second canvas. Default private; public only on explicit cue. After talk, offer QR-accessible evidence ledger for depth.

D. Demo killers, ranked
P0: projector mirrors private console because topology assumption is wrong; mic permission denied/wrong device; popup blocked; stage opens as tab/on wrong screen; audience stage cannot fullscreen remotely; venue Wi-Fi/portal/API key/quota outage; Korean STT corrupts a number/name and searches the wrong claim; public card asserts stale/contradictory evidence; operator misses approval while speaking; stale card appears after slide change; source is paywalled/JS-only/robots-blocked; WSS reconnect shows divergent revision.
P1: browser update/service-worker version skew between windows; phone pairing/login delay; battery/lock/background throttling; duplicate relative next after reconnect; external search latency tail; malicious page prompt-injects verifier; rights/license forbids displaying image; accessibility failure from unreadable/rapid updates; Windows notification or browser chrome leaks on projector.
P2: visual polish defects, optional WebRTC failure, install prompt absence. These matter far less than safe manual recovery.

E. Simpler product ladder
1) MVP “Presenter Copilot”: existing slide deck remains authoritative; private phone/laptop console shows notes, timing, Q&A prompts, and upload-time evidence. Public projector stays unchanged. No multi-display automation needed.
2) “Evidence Button”: pre-approved card deck, presenter manually invokes a card; stage receives immutable public DTO. Works offline after prefetch and is demo-safe.
3) “Live Assist”: streaming STT suggests private queries/candidates from approved corpus; no public auto-publish.
4) “Live Web Beta”: external sources, private-only, logs failures/abstentions.
5) Only after evidence: public live cards and Chromium auto-placement. Electron launcher is optional for controlled Windows fleets, not a default architecture.

F. Bounded experiments / go-no-go
E1 Setup reliability: 30 cold starts across 3 Windows versions x Chrome/Edge/Firefox x extend/mirror x popup allowed/blocked; novice gets 90s. GO if >=95% reach correct public-only stage without facilitator and zero private leaks; otherwise manual setup is the only supported contract.
E2 Recovery chaos: during 20 talks inject Wi-Fi loss, WSS drop, phone lock, screen hotplug, fullscreen exit, API timeout. GO if slide control remains locally usable, audience sees a safe holding/current slide, recovery <10s p95, zero duplicate commands/private bytes.
E3 Korean STT: 200 target utterances with names, dates, money, units, code-switching, venue noise. Gate on semantic claim accuracy, not WER. GO live search only if >=95% key entity/number/unit correctness or those errors are detected and suppressed.
E4 Verification: 300 utterances (supported/contradictory/unverifiable, time-sensitive, multi-hop). Blind human gold labels. GO if public-eligible precision >=99%, false-support <=1%, and abstention is uncapped; latency p95 <=5s only among eligible candidates. No cherry-picked demo scripts.
E5 Audience value: randomized crossover, >=60 audience members, same talk: no cards vs presenter-invoked integrated cards vs automatic second screen. Measure delayed comprehension, claim-source calibration, speaker recall, gaze switches, distraction, trust. Ship public screen only if it materially improves comprehension/calibration and does not worsen speaker recall/distraction; subjective “looks impressive” is not enough.
E6 Presenter load: >=12 presenters, rehearsal + live. Measure missed cues, approval time, speech disfluency, NASA-TLX, wrong approvals. GO if evidence controls do not worsen delivery and >=90% approvals complete without stopping speech; otherwise assign a producer role or make cards pre-approved/manual.
E7 Security: audience-role byte capture, QR race, stale-controller command, ACL revoked between retrieval/publish, malicious source prompt. GO requires zero private canary bytes, one winner per pairing, all stale/unauthorized publishes denied.
E8 Demo dress rehearsal: ten consecutive end-to-end runs on venue hardware/network with fresh profiles and no engineer intervention. One P0 failure resets the count.

Decision rule: if E4 or E5 fails, kill public live evidence—not the whole product. Preserve Presenter Copilot + pre-approved Evidence Button, which captures most value with a fraction of the epistemic and platform risk.

## EXPAND
- LEAD: Compare an even more radical “no auxiliary screen” design: subtle evidence markers embedded in the main slide plus a post-talk evidence ledger.
- LEAD: Test whether the actual buyer values trust/audit more than spectacle; procurement may prefer an exportable source ledger over live cards.
- LEAD: Define explicit kill metrics now so the team cannot rationalize a flashy but harmful second screen after building it.
- DEAD END: Treating PWA installation as a way around browser permissions or popup/fullscreen rules is refuted by the platform model.
